caption: Table 1. Resource composition and sequence-data availability.

Table 2. Molecular coverage of donor-engineering designs in the mixed-divergence scenario. Scores use the sequence-evaluable subset and weighted-divergence units. GTKO is zero only in this subset because the α-Gal axis has no sequence score; this does not imply absence of biological targeting by GGTA1 deletion. Totals are checked before independent rounding; displayed sums can differ by 0.01.
Table 3. Template-based structural comparisons at a 5 Å contact threshold. RMSD is in Å; contacts denote residue pairs.

Table 4. Published functional source-data contrasts. Treatment is 3KO.7TG minus 3KO; n=3 cell sources per group. C3b uses thousand MFI units; injury uses percentage points. CIs are approximate Welch intervals; p values are exact two-sided permutation tests.
Table S1. Sequence-feature descriptive association. Intervals condition on the selected catalogue and dependency proxy; p=NA.
Table S2. Scoring scenarios and interpretation.

Table S3. Available-sequence mixed-candidate organ strata. T/A/R in weighted-divergence units. Axis totals already include missing records; the two counts are not additive. Each of these strata contains the same 12 sequence-missing non-controls. Unrounded values satisfy T=A+R; independent rounding can produce a 0.01 display difference.
Table S4. Selected full-length sequence QC. Missing inputs remain missing; identities use paired residues.
Table S4b. Tier-2 weight sensitivity across all atlas rows. Jaccard compares unique gene pairs among the top 100 rows with the reference divergence weight 0.6.
Table S5. Exploratory antigen enrichment. The estimate and its interval refer to the stated estimand.
Table S6. Glycan-enzyme panel, separate from protein sequon priority.
Table S6b. Antigen evidence sources, measured endpoints and interpretation.
Table S7. Filter sensitivity and model confidence at 5 Å.
Table S8. Entire observed-control peptide comparison cohort. Higher score and lower rank number indicate higher priority.
Table S9. Continuous public-proteomics comparisons. Intervals are conditional protein-bootstrap ranges; NA denotes unavailable inference.
Table S10. Technical-repeat antibody-binding examples from Fig. 1b. No biological CI or p value is estimable from these triplicates.
Table S11. All published genotype contrasts. C3b is thousand MFI units; CDC is percentage points. ED4 is a separate experiment, not extra replicates for Fig. 3.
Table S12. Paired C3b blocking contrasts. Effect is blocked minus unblocked, in thousand MFI units; RI sources remain separate.
Table S13. Additional mapped peptide rows relative to primary mapping. Observed-control rows determine eligibility for the primary endpoint.
Table S14. Mapping sensitivities and primary baselines. Intervals are conditional on the supplied assay set.
Table S15. Expanded observed-control cohort under M3–M5. The additional gene is RPN1.
Table S16. Practical workflows and their interpretation.
Table S17. Scope of complementary resources and the XenoPairDB framework.
Table S18. Numerical scoring scenarios. n counts included axes, including zero-score controls. Shares use the row-specific total. Exact arithmetic is checked before independent display rounding.
Table S19. Count-based direct genetic targeting. The non-control denominator is 63; all-catalogue targeting includes 12 controls. Counts are not functional rescue fractions.

Table S20. Entire 11-axis retrospective catalogue overlap at divergence weight 0.6. Scores use a 0–100 scale. Shared gene pairs can have different directions or catalogue endpoints; opposite annotations are not resolved by the gene-pair score.

Table S21. Additional full-length sequence QC denominators for the 20-gene panel. Paired identity divides identical residues by aligned residue pairs; column identity divides by all alignment columns. Coverage divides aligned pairs by the corresponding species length. NA remains unavailable; boundary-specific results accompany the archive.

Table S22. Contact-threshold sensitivity at 8 Å. Counts are heavy-atom residue-pair contacts, not atom-pair counts. Interface pLDDT depends on the threshold-defined residue set. Principal 5 Å results remain in Table 3 and Table S7; these are geometric diagnostics.
